You need to be your favourite person. Before you call me a narcissist, hear me out:- 

World is a cold harsh place. And, people always look for a reason to beat you down: your boss, abusive relations, poor luck whatnot. 

Every time someone crushes your spirit, a little part of you dies. 
You lose confidence. And, you look for escape. 

You scroll on social media looking for hope. 
And, it mentally depresses you further. 

Someone abuses/opinions about you changes you who you are. 
You end up losing yourself. 

You look back at your life. And, realize that you changed. 
Why? because you cared more about others than you. 

But, if you are your own favourite person. You will be kind to yourself. 
You will exercise, eat right, take care, be gentle, forgive him/her for mistakes. 

***** 

Honestly the world does not care about you. 
Only you and your mom does. 

And, they are probably the only 2 people, who will be kind to you. 
Your mom will leave you one day. 
But, you will die with you. 

So by being your own favourite person, you preserve the best of you.

If you are a low energy person. And, can't do any activity outside work or school, this is for you:- 

When you can't do activities outside work/studies eg. travel, gym, singing, dancing etc. 
You have basically close to 0 personality.   

If your personality sucks, you will struggle in life. 

Moreover, at some stage in your career, promotions too become personality dominant. So you will start struggling on promotions as well. And, that is when people typically burn out. 
 
Either grow your energy.  
Or see yourself getting left behind.

**** 

Here are 3 things you can start doing today:- 

1) Improve your diet. 
2) Improve your thinking/mindset: think positive. Give yourself learning goals. When you learn something new, it improves your confidence. Confidence improves your energy. 
3) Do some low stress activities. Eg. if you can't exercise, go for a walk. If you can exercise, improve your intensity. 

Energy comes from progressive overloads on brain, body.

The worst thing middle class people do is to do the middle class things. 

This sounds confusing, so let me explain by using an example. 

The 1st major investment that a middle class family makes is a house. 
And, they do this on an EMI. 
This locks all their future earnings into 1 house. 

The house is never the problem. 
The problem is: the inability to afford that EMI. 

The race to do middle class things, actually keeps people in the middle class trap. 
Sounds weird. But, this is true. 

Best thing you can do? See what 95% middle class does. And, do the opposite. 

I'm not guaranteeing that we'd succeed. 
But, if we do things that most people do, we'd get results most people get. 

So if our goal is to be in top 1%, our only chance is to think differently.

Change your environment. And, I promise you that your life will change.   
If you want to get fit, just go to a park/gym where fit people work out. 

Maybe you are 5% at their level now.   

But, if you stay in that environment for 1 year, you grow and become 20% their level over time.   

Same applies to wealth: go and meet rich guys. 
Learn how they think. How they talk. 
How they make decisions. 
Emulate them.   

Try to live in that environment for 1 year, your decision making will improve.   

Watching podcasts, reading books and all is great. 

But, it won't fundamentally change you.   
You will only fundamentally change when you reboot your system.

1) Own a house.  
2) Own some gold.  
3) Own some US assets (Eg. US stocks). Especially AI stocks.  
4) Keep some money in cash (i.e inflation adjusted bonds).  
5) This is basically diversification which even a class 10th student can do (if he/she has the money ;) 

We are not smart enough to predict whether AI will live or die. Experts are divided.   

If it lives on, we have deflation. 
Something like gold will eventually lose value fast for a few decades.   

If it dies, the money goes to hard assets.   

Prepare your portfolio for both :)  
That's what smart investors are doing.

"Money won't make you happy"-- says every Billionaire. 

When you achieve something, 
the value of it goes down. 

Money is no different. 

If you wish to understand how important money is: 
- Ask a jobless 40 year old, who is struggling to pay EMIs. 
- Or a 25 year old grad, who could never find his first good job. 
- Or a 60 year old, with no roof over his/her head. 

Philosophy, like fine wine, is an art form enjoyed by the rich.

I get 2 job offers/day on Linkedin. 
Now, the thing is that I am not even looking for a job. 

When I was actually looking for a job, I used to write to maybe 100 firms. 
And, get 2 replies back. 

Same applies for loans. When I was actually planning an MBA abroad, I was deeply worried about my finances. 

I checked with a few banks. And, realized that I would never get the full loan amount to finance my MBA. 

Now, when I don't need any loan from any bank. 
I get 5 loan offers. 

World is a strange place. 
When you really want something. 
You won't get it. 

But, when you stop bothering, stars line up.

I was traveling in a metro. And I saw at least 95% junta scrolling reels. 

People are distracted more than ever today. 
Therefore, I think it has gotten way easier to win at anything in life. 

Of course luck plays an important role. I'm not discounting that. 
But, you can't control luck. 
However, you can scientifically control your scrolling. 

People are so busy consuming all the drama around: that they have no clue where their entire day goes. 

If you are a person with average intelligence. 
Who can avoid distractions. 
You already have an alpha.

3 months ago, I could do 0 pull-ups. 
Now, I can do 8 clean.   

I know that it doesn't mean much. 
But, it is super fun to make progress each day.   

More than anything else, it just helps you focus on good positive things in life. And, improve. 

Applies to exercising, nutrition, money, life.   
Example:-   

If you are starting with less money, it is fine; just try to be better by next year. You are not competing with Warren Buffett. 

If like me you can't do any pull ups, it is fine. You are not competing with Dwayne Johnson ('The Rock').   

Just the quest to be better than you were yesterday is a worthy goal to chase.

Increasing the **surface area of your luck** is an interesting concept:-  
 
1) In 2022, my wife and I knew no one when we moved to South Goa. 
We just packed our bags, took a chance. And, fell in love with the place.   

We got exposed to extremely clean environment.   

2) In 2024, we were tired of excessive taxation. I packed my bags. Booked an AirBnB. Moved to Dubai. Met a few folks. 

And, realized that I could actually save 2X more by living in UAE.   We got exposed to 0% taxation.  

3) In 2025, I started doing Options in the US Markets. I realized that I need to pay 0% tax. And, can net 6-8% of my cash flows by spending probably 15 mins a day.   

This was one of these easiest cash flows I ever made.  
In the process, I ended up building the biggest investment community for NRIs globally. 

4) In 2026, I started exploring more about global investing; geo-arbitrage. My family and I spend a lot of time across Goa, Dubai, South East Asia.   

We keep meeting wonderful folks. Who teach us numerous things.   

5) Every day when I get up: I make a point to go out of my house. Example: if I am living in a hotel-- I would simply get up. Go to the Gym.

Maybe in a month, I will meet 3 new folks.   
They teach me something new.   

Every action increases the surface area of your luck  The more luck you have, the better your life gets.  

The world is one big beautiful place.  And, there is so much to explore each day :)   
It all starts by getting out of your house.

Take risks while you can:- 

1) It is incredibly hard to take a loan. And, go study abroad at 20.
2) It is incredibly hard to quit your secure job at 30. And, switch careers.
3) It is incredibly hard to quit your job at 40. And, do a startup.

It never gets easier.  

1) At 20, you have less to lose. But more fear of the unknown.
2) At 30, you have more skill. But more responsibilities. 
3) At 40, you have more capital. But more inertia holding you back.

Start small when you have a chance.

1) India is expensive for the middle class. The amount of taxes % of income is fairly high.   

2) It is also expensive for the poor. Fine, yeah you can survive on freebies etc.   

But, the downside is that you existence can be erased due to brutality (eg. people driving Porsche and killing people). 

So the poor run an asymmetric risk on their literal existence.  

3) Surprisingly it is also expensive for the rich. Someone who earns 5Cr, would easily pay 1.5Cr in taxes.   

The person could live 5X better globally. And, might end up spending less.   

This is basically a broken structure, where almost no one is benefitting.   

I genuinely believe that we have a lot of potential. But, we need to change the core structure of how we think about taxes.

Guys, the price of sugar, petrol, oil everything has spiked. Then why do you think: A HOUSE that is made of brick, cement etc would suddenly start costing less?   

If the cost of transportation, raw material etc goes up by 30-40%, it is common sense to assume that the cost of construction would go up at least 50% (some commissions in between).   

This is especially true on properties where you own the land underneath. Eg. Villas.   

I started buying Villas in 2022. 
And, own several now. 
Not a single one has gone down in price.   

Yes, Real Estate (like any other asset) has cycles. And, these cycles are longer than let's say equities.  

But, do you know what Real Estate goes down in a bad cycle?   
Ans) speculative real estate.   

Eg. a builder selling you off-plan. And, pricing the properties 5 year forward prices.   Irrespective of geography, such properties go down in value. 

Not because these were 'bad' properties. But, because these were speculative properties sold on a payment plan. And, a promise of a bright future.   

If you have bought shoe in a box on the outskirts of a city on such a payment plans, you will see a correction. Probably a deep one.
